statement: Two residuals only, after the published work is subtracted. (a) Is the order in which individual laboratory rodents are caught out of a cage a REPEATABLE individual trait — an ICC or equivalent across >=5 days in individually marked cage-mates? No repeatability estimate exists for catch order; the only repeatability work is on wild-rodent trappability, a different construct, and it concluded trappability is not a personality proxy. (b) Does the group-mean shift induced by catch-order allocation, benchmarked against PUBLISHED treatment effect sizes for the same endpoints, reach the size of the effects such experiments report? Do NOT re-run the endpoint-effect measurement: Takao et al. 2016 already did it at scale.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: ARRIVE 2.0 Item 4a asserts the hazard in the field's own words ("Selecting an animal 'at random' (i.e., haphazardly or arbitrarily) from a cage is not statistically random"), names researcher judgement as the mechanism and prescribes allocation concealment, citing no measurement — https://resources.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/arrive/items/randomisation.html; NC3Rs guidance names the easier-to-catch mechanism explicitly. The endpoint half is already partly answered: Takao et al. 2016, Front Behav Neurosci 10:99, measured removal-order effects on rectal temperature, hot-plate latency, elevated-plus-maze open-arm time and plasma corticosterone in ~1,700 control C57BL/6J mice; Schipper et al. 2025 adds within-cage order effects on three behavioural tests (its Methods could not be read, so whether its "testing order" is physical catch order or a pre-assigned order is unverified). Neither reports repeatability-as-trait or the benchmark.
inputs.tier: A (limb (a) is a single-lab observational log; limb (b) is a re-analysis against published effect sizes — both cheap, neither needing new treatment arms)
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
